data: compact fossil-rich limestone with compact whitish limestone with chonchoidal fracture nodules, likely white brecciated limestone (Pellegrino FM, Crisanti FM) (grainstone with orbitolina, sparitic and recrystallized calcite and nodules of packstone with foraminifera, sponge spiculae, globigerinoids, radiolarians) (identification based on pXRF, digital microscopy, XRD, optical microscopy)

The neatly displayed material principally derives from the personal collection of a Librarian of Marsala (Salvatore Struppa) who also become honorary inspector of antiquities of the region. The ceramics mostly derive from early Lilybaeum (4-2 centuries BC) some architectural pieces and uninscribed cinerary urns. A stretch of 5th century AD road has been excavated and is on display in one room, and an entire room is given over to 8 Latin inscriptions from Lilybaeum

English translation

Giorgia Capra

To the emperor Caesar, our lord Flavius Valens, pious, fortunate, forever Augustus; Marcus Valerius Quintianus, vir clarissimus, governor (consularis) of the province of Sicily, forever most dedicated to his clemency and piety.

Italian translation

Giorgia Capra

All'imperatore Cesare, il nostro patrono Flavius Valens, pio, fortunato, sempre Augusto; Marcus Valerius Quintianus, vir clarissimus, governatore della provincia di Sicilia, per sempre consacratissimo alla sua pietà e clemenza.
